result.title: MOBO-CAPS: Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization with Cardinality-Aware Pareto Selection
result.summary: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) traditionally aims to approximate the entire Pareto front, but, due to resource constraints, real-world deployment is often limited to testing a small, representative subset of solutions. Hence current methods first approximate the full front before selecting solutions, potentially wasting costly evaluations. We formalize this problem as Multi-objective Bayesian Optimization with Cardinality-aware Pareto Selection (MOBO-CAPS), where the goal is to identify a set of exactly M solutions with high hypervolume. We propose two practical cardinality-aware acquisition strategies: REHVI, a replacement-aware approximation to expected hypervolume improvement, and CHO-UCB, which constructs an optimistic M-point set by optimizing a collective UCB-based hypervolume objective. We prove a sublinear simple regret bound for the batched version of CHO-UCB, and empirically show that cardinality-aware acquisition design improves over standard MOBO followed by post-hoc subset selection across nine benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文把「最终只需交付固定 M 个高 hypervolume 解」的情形形式化为 MOBO-CAPS，提出两种直接面向基数约束下取值的采集策略 REHVI 与 CHO-UCB，并给出批量版 CHO-UCB 的次线性简单遗憾界与九个基准上的经验对比。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是为固定大小的最终解集直接设计采集目标、而非优化完整前沿再事后筛选，这一「价值驱动、预算受限下的定容子集选择」视角可能可供核查到 LVR 中证据／latent 假设的有限容量筛选与评估预算分配问题。
